newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end firmer, helped by Wall St gains.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end firmer, helped by Wall St gains.

text.p: French shares closed higher on Monday, supported by a rise on Wall Street, but volume was thin in part because London was closed for a market holiday.

The bourse also got a boost from a BVA poll putting the centre-right coalition in a comfortable-but-reduced lead over the Socialists after weekend polls showing their margin shrinking. Prime Minister Alain Juppe said he thought the election contest was getting closer.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 17.53 points or 0.66 percent at 2,672.84, while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 24 at 2,662 from Friday's close.
Volume was a moderate 4.6 billion francs.

A Louis Harris poll, published after the market close, showed the left gaining ground, with 45 percent of people polled wanting a Socialist/Communist win, against 43 percent wanting a conservative victory.
Shares in Paribas, which went ex-dividend, gained 3.11 percent to 371.80. It also benefited from a broker upgrade.

Thomson-CSF shares rose 2.33 percent to 184.20 francs, helped by newspaper reports Dasa of Germany was talking to rival bidders Lagardere and Alcatel Alsthom about possible cooperation after the privatisation. Lagardere shares closed down 0.55 percent at 180 francs, while Alcatel rose 0.47 percent to 645.
Hotel group Accor denied market talk that it was looking to sell its U.S.-based Motel 6 chain. "It's the same old rumour from the same broker looking to push stock," said one trader.
Renault rose 3.43 percent to 141.7 francs, benefiting from French car sales figures last week which showed it outperforming the market.
A broker said the stock performed poorly last year and was due for a rise on its restructuring and on the positive effects seen from product launches.
